trust_decision.summary: Part-header bytes from the multipart body are untrusted: a header line containing a bare CR or LF must not be parsed at all (deps/dicer/lib/HeaderParser.js), and a Content-Disposition name/filename must not be handed to the field/file callbacks if it still contains CR/LF after parseParams percent-decoding (lib/types/multipart.js) - the rule therefore has to hold at two layers, in two packages.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names multipart Content-Disposition filename and name, and this is the only loop that assigns fieldname/filename from parsed Content-Disposition parameters before they are emitted to the field/file callbacks.

fix_sites.entry_point: part 'header' event consumed at lib/types/multipart.js:111, and the public Busboy.Dicer export (index.js:85) which emits parsed part headers at deps/dicer/lib/Dicer.js:42-45
fix_sites.module_kind: vendored dependency / lower-level header parser, deps/dicer/

fix_sites.entry_point: same multipart field/file callbacks; helper added next to skipPart (lib/types/multipart.js:295-297)
fix_sites.module_kind: helper function in the multipart type handler

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: deps/dicer/lib/HeaderParser.js:108-142 (reached from lib/types/multipart.js:85 and from the public Busboy.Dicer export at index.js:85)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: deps/dicer is a vendored copy of the standalone dicer parser, and the advisory names only multipart Content-Disposition name/filename, so a solver can argue the header-level CR/LF rule belongs upstream and that the mimeType / transfer-encoding values built from those headers are not the reported fields.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: RFC2822 folded header continuation lines must keep being joined into the previous value, and the maxHeaderSize truncation path must still emit the header map; a fix that rejects the whole header buffer for containing '\r' or that throws instead of dropping the offending pair breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: name="field\rname" and name="field\nname" (bare CR or LF inside a quoted name)
filename="file\rname.txt" and filename="file\nname.txt" (bare CR or LF inside a quoted filename)
name*=utf-8''field%0Dname and name*=utf-8''field%0Aname (RFC 2231 extended parameter; CR/LF appear only after parseParams percent-decoding)
bare CR/LF in a part header name or in any header value at the dicer layer, e.g. 'Foo\rbad: bar', 'Foo: bar\rbare', 'Foo\nbad: bar'

O8b_injection_room.sibling: CR/LF rejection inside the fast quoted form-data disposition parser instead of at its caller
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: parseParams is also called from index.js:55 for the top-level Content-Type, so a maintainer hardening the producer would place the rule here to cover every caller at once.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: CR/LF rejection on percent-decoded urlencoded field names before boy.emit('field', ...)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: urlencoded field names arrive on the same 'field' callback contract and are percent-decoded the same way, so a maintainer listing protected name fields would mirror the multipart check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: CR/LF rejection on the Content-Type charset parameter parsed from the part header
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: charset is also produced by parseParams from an untrusted part header and is what decodeText uses for the emitted value, so it sits on the same sink path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: parsing and filtering trailer header bytes before emitting 'trailer'
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: trailers are the one remaining block of raw header bytes handed to consumers without going through HeaderParser.

O9_family: CRLF injection (CWE-93) - unvalidated CR/LF in multipart part-header parameters reaching user-visible fieldname/filename values

O10_build.toolchain: npm; node --test wrapped by c8 with a 100% statement/branch/function/line coverage gate; tstyche for types; eslint/neostandard
O10_build.project_tests: test/dicer-headerparser.test.js requires deps/dicer/lib/HeaderParser directly (line 4) and table-drives header parsing; test/types-multipart-coverage.test.js and test/types-multipart.test.js drive Busboy multipart bodies; test/parse-params.test.js covers parseParams; all node:test, no network

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject or strip CR/LF only in the lib/types/multipart.js disposition loop (or only test the quoted plain-string shape), leaving deps/dicer/lib/HeaderParser.js and the percent-decoded RFC 2231 shape open.

out_of_scope_notes: lib/types/urlencoded.js:138,176 emit percent-decoded field names to the same 'field' callback, so %0D/%0A in a urlencoded body name also reaches a header-injectable value; same class but outside this advisory's multipart Content-Disposition scope, not pursued.
